# 2D sprite generation through an MCP (SpriteCook, Pixel Engine, AutoSprite, any other)

**When it applies:** every 2D game whose sprites, props, tiles, UI pieces or FX are generated by an agent through an image tool's MCP. The method below is tool independent; what each tool offers and where it bites is in [per-tool-notes.md](per-tool-notes.md). It does not cover Makko: Makko has no MCP and is driven in Chrome by `Letta/Skills/Skill 27 - Makko Operator/`, with its sheets imported by `references/sprite-animation-import/`.

**Where it comes from.** Overdue (SpriteCook long 8, 2026-10-23, Godot 4.7.2, SpriteCook plugin 0.1.15) is the build whose art came out best: 125 shipped stills, every one at one pixel density, nothing rescaled, 4,757 credits in V1 plus 364 in V2. Marco asked for this module after it (2026-10-25: the SpriteCook art "came out super well"). Its sources, all in `D:\_Programming\Game Development\Games - Letta Collaborations\SpriteCook\8 - Overdue\`: `docs/MCP_NOTES.md` (probes, models), `docs/BUILD_NOTES.md` (directives, credit waves, Visual mismatches, Manual fixes), `docs/Overdue - Build GDD.md` §11 (the pipeline), `docs/v2/lane-*.md` (V2 art), `tools/` (the scripts named below). The AutoSprite and Pixel Engine builds (Last Floor Hotel, Stormfield Fighters, Critter Camp, Duckling Detour) supply the counter examples.

The thesis, in Kimo's words as recorded in Overdue (SpriteCook's founder, 2026-10-23): **any resolution, but never scale generated pixel art up or down, and the pixel size of every asset must match.** Everything below is how a build keeps that promise across a hundred or more jobs.

---

## 1. One pixel density for the whole game, decided and probed before any wave

- ⛔ **k = 1 in every shipped file:** one image pixel is one art pixel. k is the block size, the most common length of a run of identical colour along rows and columns (ignore the 1 px outline antialias). A tool that draws chunky pixels at k = 2 or 3 has not given you an asset yet.
- ⛔ **One display scale for the whole game, the same for every asset.** Overdue renders natively at 1920x1080 at scale 1, so one art pixel is one screen pixel at 1080p (Marco, 09:47: "something like HD pixel art like 128x128"; Remy 128 px tall, cell 96 px, every gameplay number times 3). Critter Camp and Duckling Detour (Pixel Engine) used one art pixel = 2 screen pixels, sprites at scale 2.0 with Nearest, "never fractional". Either works; mixing does not.
- ⛔ **Never resample a generated asset to fix its size.** An asset outside its size tolerance is regenerated at the right size, never rescaled. Overdue shipped zero rescaled files. The only exception in the Overdue GDD (§11.4 step 2) is lossless: an image that is a clean grid of k by k blocks may be divided by exactly k with nearest neighbour to recover k = 1. Overdue never needed it, because every shipped still came from an exact size model.
- **Decide the density from the outputs, never from the concept image.** A concept is not pixel art (every pixel unique), so it cannot tell you the grid. Cogwood got the base resolution wrong three times by deriving it from the concept (Skill 6.1 `style-guide.md` §3d). Generate the hero first, measure it, and derive the cell and the view from it: hero about 13 to 15 percent of screen height, 2 to 3 tiles tall.
- **Probe the size control of every tool and model before the first wave** (Overdue GDD §11.14). Ask each candidate for one 48x48 and one 96x64 still, then the largest size you need, with smart crop off. A tool has exact size control only if every raw file comes back at exactly the requested dimensions and k = 1. Overdue's probe (09:35 to 09:41, under 100 credits): `pixel-engine-image-v1` exact at 48x48, 96x64, 40x48, 106x128, 86x128, 128x128, 128x86 and unable to go past 128; `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` in density mode ignored the hint (48x48 asked, 129x124 back; 96x64 gave 272x254; 112x144 gave 34x34). Record the finding per tool, dated, in `docs/MCP_NOTES.md`.
- **Re-list the models at every wave** (`list_generation_models` or the tool's equivalent) and record it. Rule 1d of `SKILL.md` covers updating the plugin first.

## 2. Anchors first, then a style check, then waves

1. **Upload the concept as the first asset** (`anchor_concept`) when the tool takes references.
2. **The hero anchor** (`anchor_remy` in Overdue), then **one prop and one tile per zone** (`anchor_s`, `anchor_b`, `anchor_v`). Everything after follows them.
3. **One animation test on the hero** (Overdue: `remy idle`, 4 frames, 20 credits) to prove the animation tool keeps the density.
4. **A style check before any bulk generation:** the anchors and the test side by side with the concept, plus the audit scripts (Overdue `tools/audit_density.py`, `audit_palette.py`, `audit_animation.py`, each with negative controls). In Overdue V1 that check passed at 10:00, 28 minutes in, and only then did waves 1 to 5 run (131 still jobs, 4 parallel agents, done at 10:33).
5. **Families do not drift.** A family (a character and all its clips, a zone and its props, the UI set, the time objects) uses one model, one quality and one reference set, generated in one wave (GDD §11.14). A model change mid build means regenerating the family or logging a Visual mismatch.

## 3. The prompt: a short style lock plus a strict view lock

- **One short style lock, the same sentence in every prompt, with zone variants.** Overdue's long lock (about 600 characters) made `pixel-engine-image-v1` refuse every job (failed and refunded; under about 560 passed), so the build used this one:

  > HD pixel art, crisp pixels, thin dark outline, flat 2D side view, [zone palette words], no text, transparent background.

- ⛔ **A strict view lock in every prompt** (Overdue `AGENTS.md` rule 4, Marco 11:52 on the checkout counter: "be careful that some assets are isometric and not side/front view"): every asset is a pure side profile or a straight on front elevation with the camera level, never three quarter, isometric or top down, no visible top surface of boxes and counters, no slanted sides. The models drift into three quarter by default; the lock has to be in the prompt, not assumed.
- **Subject first, then size, then the lock.** In exact size mode: "Exactly [W] by [H] pixels, one art pixel per pixel." In density mode: "Draw it on a coarse grid of about W by H pixels." (GDD §11.12, prompt templates per class: still, parallax layer, character base, character clip, tileset, FX sheet).
- **Prompt suffixes leak into the subject.** AutoSprite Last Floor Hotel: a "warm candlelight" suffix put candles into every draft of the cat, the service bell and the fence; "gothic monster hotel" turned cornices into building facades; Stormfield's "night storm" painted a storm inside the torii gate. Keep the lock to style, view and background words, never mood or setting nouns.
- **Name only what should be there.** Naming an unwanted thing ("no wings", "feet stay hidden") tends to make it appear (AutoSprite tool guidance; measured on Duckling Detour: Pixel Engine v1.5 drew feet on the swimming ranger in 4 of 8 and 6 of 8 frames despite "feet stay hidden").
- **Multi object sheets** need "every object separate, nothing touching, generous empty space" or the alpha welds them (Skill 6.1 §6b: counting alpha islands predicted the slicer's output exactly, 11/13/14/10/10).

## 4. The view audit: budget it, it is not free

What Overdue measured: **71 of 125 shipped stills came back three quarter or isometric.** The audit and its cost:

- **Three independent judges, majority vote.** Contact sheets of every still (`docs/evidence/view-audit/sheet-01.png` to `-05.png` with `index.json`); an asset is flagged when 2 of 3 judges call it three quarter, isometric or top down.
- **Every flagged asset is regenerated at the same size with the strict view lock**, reviewed before and after (`after-01.png` to `-08.png`, `after-index.json`). Two rounds: 65 of 71 ended flat. Six stayed three quarter because Pixel Engine kept drawing their top faces (`to_crusher`, `to_crumble`, `to_crumble_cracked`, `to_plate_up`, `to_plate_down`, `mountain_chunk_a`); each pair keeps one consistent view and they are listed under Visual mismatches.
- ⛔ **Cost: 2,336 credits against 300 to 500 planned, 49 percent of the V1 spend.** The fixers ran two variations per job (12 credits instead of 6) and up to four tries per asset, plus 160 credits on two Nano Banana Pro retries of the counter. What to do next time: the view lock in the FIRST prompt of every asset, the audit on each wave rather than at the end, one variation per corrective retry, a hard cap of two tries per asset, and the audit as its own line in the credit plan.
- Some objects resist a flat view and need a different subject, not more tries. Overdue's stair steps: the regenerated `to_step_*` drew small runs of stairs; V2 replaced them with a square tread block that fills its cell (`to_tread`, 96x96), so the art is exactly the collision box (`docs/v2/lane-D.md`: try 1 drew a staircase shape again, try 2 variation 1 was isometric, variation 2 was used).

## 5. Pick the model per asset class by measured result

- **Probe the same prompt on the candidates and look.** Overdue 11:10, the Showroom back wall, 4K 16:9, `pixel` on, three Pixel Engine props as style references: Nano Banana Pro (`gemini-3-pro-image`) 40 credits, 408x245, k = 1, flat side view, VHS spines 4 to 5 px wide like the references (same pixel size); Nano Banana 2.1, 30 credits, 480x268, k = 1, but a room interior in perspective that does not tile.
- **The resulting rule in Overdue:** Pixel Engine Image for everything up to 128 px per side (exact size, native transparency, 6 credits); Nano Banana Pro with Pixel Engine assets as style references for single pieces between 128 and 512 px (its size hint caps at 512); anything bigger is composed from pieces (§8). Marco's first call (10:12, "the best seems to be pixel engine image, just use that one") was relaxed at 11:08 to "see which one allows you to create better stuff visually" under Kimo's no scaling rule.
- **Reject a model whose sizes you cannot predict**, even if its pictures are pretty: Sunburst in density mode returned 34 to 503 px for similar requests and shipped nothing in Overdue.
- **Style references set the pixel size more than any size hint.** A model that cannot hit an exact size can still land on the anchor's density when the anchor is its style reference (Overdue: Sunburst with the Remy anchor as the only reference drew at Remy's pixel size). Verify k and size anyway.

## 6. Look at every result before using it

- **Every result is opened and looked at at 1:1 and at a nearest neighbour zoom before it ships.** Every V2 lane report of Overdue ends with "every result was looked at before use". What looking caught that no script did: the Standee boss drew a famous hero look alike and repeated the fists (regenerated); the robot pelvis drew two boots; the robot upper arm came back three quarter with a neighbour cut in; the thigh drew a side view lower leg; the icon `ui_icon_rewind` variation a had a stray spike.
- **When two variations are paid for, choose by eye on the real background** (lane B chose each HUD icon on the actual button plate).

## 7. The paper trail: raws, records, manifest, credits

- **Raw plus a json record per job, the raw never edited.** Overdue's `tools/sc_record.py` downloads to `assets/spritecook/raw/<id>.png` and writes `<id>.json` with the tool's asset id, job id, kind, model, wave, credits, the full prompt, the parameters, bytes and the UTC time. Any asset can be regenerated or edited from its record. Rejected variants go to `raw/_probe/<lane>/` as evidence, never deleted silently.
- **An asset manifest is the source of truth** (`data/asset_manifest.json`: id, class, zone, model, target W and H, wave, prompt). `tools/sc_batch.py` records a batch, writes the processed copy (a byte copy of the raw for exact size stills) and a contact sheet at 2x, and flags any size that differs from the target. Trap from V2: a manifest generator that rebuilds the file from its own tables silently drops rows added by hand; add new rows to the generator.
- **A credit ledger per wave with a hard ceiling and a cut order.** `get_credit_balance` (or the tool's equivalent) before and after every wave; a planning estimate per wave replaced after wave 1 by the measured cost per class times the count; the projected total recomputed before every wave; past the threshold, cut non hero assets first and hero assets last (GDD §11.0 step 5). Overdue V1: ceiling 5,000, spent 4,757; V2 lanes each had a cap (A 250, B 150, C 450, D 60, E 150, F 0) and spent 364 in total, matching the balance drop exactly.
- **Cost statements follow Marco's order:** measured credits first, the flat subscription second, any API price equivalent last and labelled as not paid.

## 8. Logged deterministic repairs: crop, never rescale

- **Allowed:** deterministic scripts in `tools/` (alpha cutoff, pivot and canvas alignment, crop of stray pixels and padding to a shared cell, palette snap within a distance cap, outline normalization that only thins, thickens or closes gaps of at most 2 px) and a logged coordinate list for a stray pixel. **Not allowed:** drawing new shapes, painting a sprite by code, editing the raw (GDD §11.15).
- **Every repair has a row** with the asset, the raw, the fix and why. Overdue's five: `s_carpet_band` cropped x 17 to 113 to one 96 px cell (the slanted ends did not tile); `s_support` cropped to 127x98 so it tiles; `to_spike_off` built from the extended spike's own base strip placed on a 96x36 canvas (the regenerated retracted plate stayed isometric); `s_checkout_counter` cropped from 240x240 to its art bounds 240x126 (the empty rows would have sunk a bottom anchored prop into the floor); `to_cart` and `to_basin` installed as is with the scene's region and offsets moved to meet the collision tops.
- **Prefer a crop or an offset over a repair, and a regeneration with a corrective line over either** when the fix is not lossless.

## 9. Animations: from a still base that keeps its density

- **Animate the approved still, not a new character.** In Overdue `generate_character` had no size control (Remy at 107 px on a 110 px canvas, a density different from the anchor), so every character base is a Pixel Engine still and every clip is `animate_game_art` with `pixel-engine-v1.1` on it: frames are the source plus `edge_margin` (68x68 frames from a 40x48 source, Remy still 48 px tall in every frame, k = 1). The robot boss's legs, the Agent's walk and the fireball loop all followed the same route.
- **Even frame counts on v1.1-style engines** (2 to 16), and a hard cap on the whole animation budget (Overdue: 30 clips and 140 frames at most; reuse by flip, tint and tween, never by generating variants).
- **The starting still must already be in the starting pose of the motion** (a mid stride still for a walk loop, a curled still for a sleeping loop). For motions that reach outward, give the engine room (SpriteCook `edge_margin`, Pixel Engine `canvas` 1.3 to 1.8, AutoSprite `pad_character`).
- ⛔ **Check every frame for hallucinated extra objects and broken cycles.** What Overdue shipped and Marco caught in his V1 playtest: frame 2 of `remy/toss` drew a ghost arm holding a cassette, and frame 3 had no Remote in the hand (fixed by re-keying the shoot pose onto the existing `remote` sheet, no credits); the Agent's walk was half a step (frame 0 stands, frames 1 to 3 move only the right leg, then it snaps back), regenerated as an 8 frame two step cycle from the same 86x128 still (20 credits), with frames 4 and 5 moved down by a whole pixel to sit on the feet row; the jump clips read badly in motion, so rising holds one static frame (`jump_up` frame 1) and falling another (`fall` frame 0), with the landing squash kept. Other builds, same family of defects: Pixel Engine otter turning sideways with its tail flipping sides, a duckling back idle that turns to show its face, loops whose last to first jump was 2.17 to 2.62 times a normal step (Duckling Detour); AetherAI trailing frames that changed the character into another eagle, kept only frames 1 to 23 (`Letta/Skills/aether-clean-sprite-sheets/`).
- **Audit numbers, then eyes.** Overdue's `tools/audit_animation.py` checks per clip: no empty frame, no two identical consecutive frames, pivot jitter at most 1 px and height change at most 2 px on loops, foot line stable within 1 px on grounded loops, the loop seam at most 1.25 times the largest neighbour step, facing right in every frame. Then a contact sheet of every frame, looked at.
- **A clip that cannot be fixed cheaply becomes a still or a tween.** The Standee boss clips were native tweens at 0 credits; the stair rebuild, freeze tint, speed lines, doors, glows and every particle were native Godot (GDD §11.8). Generated alpha is binary on SpriteCook, so soft glows, trails and fades are never generated art (Skill 6.1 §6c).
- **Import:** one strip per clip, loop on for continuous clips and off for gating ones, per clip canvas and offset checked against one ground line, both facings tested: `references/sprite-animation-import/` §2 to §7.

## 10. Strips, tiles and transparency

- **Every strip or tile that repeats gets a tiling check** (place it three times side by side and look at the seams). Overdue: `to_crusher_rod` failed twice and ships with its ends cropped; 8 of 21 parallax pieces were rejected for seams or borders; the tileset's carpet came back as a 10 px strip, so a separate carpet band piece was laid along every ledge top.
- **Prefer native transparency over background removal.** Pixel Engine Image returns the background already removed; removal elsewhere erases pale or white interiors (AutoSprite: speech bubble, feather, banner crest, slash arc; Pixel Engine: mushroom stems, daisy petals, an iris losing 55 percent of its pixels). When removal is needed, ask for an off white fill instead of white, run the tool's alpha cutoff comparison (SpriteCook `get_asset_metadata.alpha_editing` then `set_asset_alpha_cutoff`, 0 credits), or key locally from the border and log it (Stormfield `local_matte`, tolerance 40, 0 credits).
- **Texture filter Nearest everywhere for pixel art**, no mipmaps; Linear only for detailed (non pixel) art.

## 11. Big assets: compose from pieces, or rig a giant from parts

- **Anything larger than the exact size model's cap is composed of pieces at the same density, never one smaller image scaled up.** Overdue: the bosses, the giant return slot, the Late Fee mountain (two chunks) and the parallax layers were assembled from Pixel Engine pieces of 128 px or less; a full 1920 wide layer stays a composition.
- **A giant boss is a parts rig.** Overdue V2's robot is 330 px tall (3.4 cells) in a strict front elevation built from Pixel Engine parts (torso 128x112, head 88x72, core 56x56, forearm 64x104, shin 48x96, foot 88x40, thigh 48x80, arm 56x88, shockwave 96x64), each 128 px or less, **never scaled and never rotated: every pose is a translation**, so one art pixel stays one screen pixel. 128 credits including the 20 credit Agent walk; 4 of 13 part jobs were rejected on sight (a pelvis with two boots, a three quarter upper arm, a thigh drawn as a lower leg, a pair of boots) and the arm was used cropped.

## 12. Timeouts: the job may still be running

- ⛔ **A tool timeout is not a failed job.** SpriteCook pixel animations exceeded the MCP timeout and every one still finished (Skill 15.1 finding 7); a guided run cut by the client timeout stopped (finding 14); Pixel Engine returned "pending" twice and both jobs completed and charged 26 credits each (Duckling Detour); AutoSprite jobs queue behind the web app for minutes "while still progressing".
- **Before resubmitting, look at what already exists:** SpriteCook `list_recent_assets` and `list_active_jobs`, Pixel Engine `list_recent_jobs` and `get_job`, AutoSprite `get_job_status` (poll at most every 30 s) and an `idempotencyKey` on retries. Paying twice for one asset is the most avoidable cost in the ledger.
- **Concurrency limits reject, they do not queue.** AutoSprite refused 5 packs at its 36 packs in flight limit (not charged, resubmitted); SpriteCook allows 10 concurrent jobs on Marco's plan. Run waves in batches under the limit.

## 13. Checklist before the art is called done

- [ ] Tool updated and models listed, dated, in `docs/MCP_NOTES.md`; size control probed per tool and model.
- [ ] One density: every shipped file at k = 1, one display scale for the whole game, zero resampled files.
- [ ] Anchors and the animation test passed the style check before the first wave.
- [ ] Short style lock and strict view lock in every prompt; the view audit run per wave, its credits in the plan.
- [ ] Every result looked at; raws plus json records kept; the manifest matches the shipped files; the credit ledger closes against the balance.
- [ ] Every repair logged (crop, offset, cutoff), none rescales.
- [ ] Every clip audited by numbers and checked frame by frame for extra objects, design drift and broken loops.
- [ ] Every repeating strip and tile checked for seams; transparency clean on light and dark backgrounds.
- [ ] Big assets composed or rigged from same density pieces; no image scaled up.
- [ ] No job paid twice after a timeout.
